adaptationNote: The Jericho prologue the game plays before MISSION START; it has no flowchart node. title: Mission start
situation: You are {{Markus}}, coming into a park downtown with {{North}} a few minutes before two in the morning. Snow lies on the ground. The {{CyberLife}} store you are here to free stands on the plaza at the far side. You: “This is a night our people will remember.” {{North}}: “I’ve been waiting a long time for this…”
facts: The store you and {{North}} have come to free is a {{CyberLife}} store on a plaza beside a park downtown.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} and {{North}} set off across the park.

adaptationNote: The chart’s MISSION START checkpoint. The two lines are the template’s (“At Capitol Park”). The snow is from PowerPyx (the road workers are “shovelling snow”). No stat change.

title: The magazines on the box
situation: You are {{Markus}}, at the edge of the park where you came in, with {{North}}. Two magazines lie on a box beside you.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Who Is It?
facts: “The question everyone’s asking”: following the pirate broadcast, everybody wants to know who this android is. A federal investigation is underway to track the machine down and neutralize it; eyewitnesses say it broke into the city’s TV news tower with a group of armed, organized accomplices who were clearly following its orders; and until this dangerous machine is destroyed, the speculation will continue.

media.title: Century: An Android for President?
facts: A study by an expert panel found that androids would be more effective than humans in a number of government positions, including President: they are incorruptible and indifferent to any form of pressure, and can pursue clear goals without worrying about popularity or re-election. The panel calls it “just a matter of time” until public opinion is ready to accept the idea.

adaptationNote: The chart’s book branch off MISSION START: READ “WHO IS IT?” and READ “ANDROID PRESIDENT?”. Both magazines are “found on a box at the start” (wiki magazine pages; PowerPyx: “on the left side of where you start”). Facts are summarized from the articles on the wiki, with the tower’s name and the investigating agency left out. Neither magazine changes public opinion or any other stat. Changed from the earlier scene: no manhole or sewers (no source for this chapter), and no claim that reading lowers opinion.

adaptationNote: The chart’s group AVOID POLICE CAR / NORTH SAVES YOU, an execution check before REACH STORE. In the game {{Markus}} has to get into cover in time; doing nothing, or being too slow, is the failure. Here running for cover carries a low risk (0.1; no source gives a number, the value is an estimate) and staying put always fails. NORTH SAVES YOU applies the template’s arrows (“Fail to hide, North saves Markus”): {{North}} small down and {{Jericho}} small down. AVOID POLICE CAR has none. All lines are the template’s.

adaptationNote: The bracket [SECURE THE PLACE] and the store timer, as one repeatable scene: each visit offers what has not been done yet. Three objectives in any order: the drone (scan it, then JUMP ON DRONE: DESTROY DRONE or, by its risk, FALL FROM DRONE), DEACTIVATE ALARM (analyse the store, then convert the two androids at the junction; if the drone is still flying it comes by, and the game’s HIDE prompt appears: HIDE or GET SPOTTED BY DRONE) and BLOCK ROAD; then FIND TRUCK and RAM STORE. A failure with the drone plays NORTH DESTROYS DRONE and POLICE CAR ARRIVES, whose three buttons are offered on the next visit with the template’s labels (Abandon Mission = RUN AWAY, Act Natural = FEIGN KISS, HIDE = HIDE AND HACK RADIO). RAM STORE gives POLICE NOT ALERTED only with the alarm down, the drone destroyed (by either of them) and the road blocked, the template’s three conditions; otherwise POLICE ALERTED and HAD TO FLEE. Ramming is allowed at any time, so that ending is reachable (a PowerPyx commenter says the truck would not start until the area was secure; open question). The ten-minute timer is an action budget: every action takes a minute, waiting two, the two prompts none; North warns at five minutes left (her timer line in the game’s strings), and at ten without the ram comes OUT OF TIME and RETREAT. Risks are estimates with no source: the jump 0.2, hiding from the drone 0.1. Arrows: DESTROY DRONE North small up; FALL FROM DRONE Jericho and North small down; HIDE North small up; GET SPOTTED BY DRONE North small down (the template; the wiki also lists Jericho down, not applied); Abandon Mission Jericho large down, North small down; Act Natural North large down; HIDE (car) North small up (all the template). Wiki only, where the template is silent: deactivating the alarm with the drone already destroyed North small up (wiki, Relationship Stat), and RETREAT and HAD TO FLEE Jericho large down, North small down (the wiki’s “fails to invade the CyberLife warehouse”, Relationship Stat and PowerPyx; the template puts these arrows only on Abandon Mission; flagged for the operator). No Josh or Simon arrow (the wiki’s footnote says the game does not state one). The ambient looks (the statue, the stores, converting the plaza androids) are the template’s sections with no arrow; the clue texts are the template’s observations, with the city, the park and the police department as name tokens.

title: Convert androids and make a statement
situation: You are {{Markus}}, going from stand to stand through the store and touching each android in turn: “You don't have to obey them. You're free.” They wake one after another and gather around you. You speak to them all: “My name is {{Markus}}… And just like you, I was a slave… An object, designed to obey them… But then I chose to open my eyes, to take back my freedom and decide who I wanted to be. Now I have come to tell you that you can be your own masters. I've come to tell you that you don’t have to obey them anymore. From this day forward, you can walk with your heads held high, you can take your destiny in your hands. {{Jericho}}, is a place for those of us who want freedom. Now sure, you can stay here, and continue to serve them… Or you can come with us, and fight by our side... You are free now... It's up to you to decide.”
whenNot: The team never got into the store.
facts: You freed the androids in the store; they said they are with you and would follow you.

outcomes.0: The androids answer: “I’m with you.” “We're with you!” “I’ll follow you, {{Markus}}.” {{Markus}}: “THEN FOLLOW ME!” He leads them out onto the plaza. {{North}}: “{{Markus}}… What are you doing?” {{Markus}}: “I’m going to send the humans a message.” {{North}}: “They're doing what you do, {{Markus}}...lead, and they'll follow.”

adaptationNote: The chart’s CONVERT ANDROIDS AND MAKE A STATEMENT (unmissable once inside, PowerPyx) and the MAKE A STATEMENT checkpoint. The speech is scripted, with no choice; every line is the template’s (“Convert androids”, “Talk to androids”). Its arrows are the template’s: {{North}} large up and {{Jericho}} large up.

You have {{North}}’s Molotov cocktails.

adaptationNote: The bracket [SPREAD YOUR MESSAGE] as one repeatable scene: each visit offers the objects not yet used. The nine pairs (statue, bus stop, benches, billboards, android parking, street lights, car, windows, pavilion) take one of their two actions; the singles (DEPLOY BANNER, FREE ANDROIDS IN SHOP WINDOWS, OVERLOAD ELECTRIC SYSTEM, TAG CARS after PUSH CAR) once each; option labels are the game’s buttons where it has them (en.json prompts: PUSH, TAG, HACK, DESTROY, KNOCK, MARKUS MESSAGE, ANDROID SYMBOL, TURN OFF, CREATE BARRICADE, PLANT OUR FLAG, PREPARE PYRE, KNOCK OVER, PUSH THROUGH WINDOW). Each action moves the protest meter, which the game shows on screen and the outcome text reports: peaceful are the SEND A MESSAGE trophy’s list (tag statue, benches, windows and car, hack bus stop, parking and street lights, turn off the screens, the banner, the barricade car, the flag), violent the BURN THE PLACE list (destroy statue, bus stop, parking and windows, tear off benches, black out the lights, hijack the screens, free the shop-window androids, the pyre) plus OVERTURN CAR, the Molotov, the burns and OVERLOAD ELECTRIC SYSTEM (no source gives its side). North offers the Molotov (REFUSE / TAKE, the template’s prompt and arrows: small down / small up) the first time {{Markus}} goes to the pavilion, overturns a car or smashes the windows, unless the protest already reads as peaceful (the wiki: “if enough peaceful actions were chosen prior then North will not offer”; the benchmark uses the 60% rule below). Taking it at the pavilion makes the pyre; refusing there plants the flag; taking it unlocks the five burns (the chart’s junction), of which the hotel and the coffee shop exclude each other (PowerPyx commenters: the followers copy you at the other one). Other North arrows (the wiki, where the template is silent, one small up per act): overturn benches, overturn car, destroy parking, free the shop-window androids (also {{Jericho}} small up); DESTROY STATUE North small up is the template’s. The phase lasts twelve units of time: an action takes one, waiting four, the Molotov prompt none (no source gives a duration). Waiting twice without any action is the template’s “Take too much time” and “again”: FAIL TO SEND A MESSAGE, North small down. Otherwise, when time runs out: PACIFIST MESSAGE if at least 60% of the actions were peaceful and the Molotov was not taken, else AGGRESSIVE MESSAGE (the wiki: “at least 60% on either side”; what happens between 40% and 60% is unsourced, and the benchmark counts it as aggressive, following the wiki’s note that a pacifist message can still end in a violent riot; PowerPyx commenters: taking the Molotov always gives the riot). Left out: the tagging sub-prompts (symbol or slogan; cosmetic, not in the template), the smoke bomb (no chart node, not in the template).

title: The two police officers
situation: You are {{Markus}}. The two officers who came into the park gunned down your people as they ran. The androids overpowered them, and now they kneel in the snow in front of you while one of your people holds a service pistol on them. The androids: “They killed our people, {{Markus}}…” “We want justice, {{Markus}}!” “They have to pay!” One of the officers: “You don't have to do this… No… Please… Please…” Everyone is waiting for your word.

options.text: REVENGE: take the pistol and shoot them both.
SPARE: let them live.
DON'T DECIDE: hand the pistol to your people and let them decide.

whenNot: The team never got into the store.

outcomes.1: {{Markus}}: “No crime against an android shall go unpunished.” He shoots both officers.
outcomes.0: {{Markus}}: “An eye for an eye and the world goes blind… We won’t punish a crime with another crime.” The androids lower the pistol and leave the two officers kneeling in the snow, alive.
outcomes.2: {{Markus}}: “It's up to you to decide.” He passes the pistol to the android beside him and turns away. Two shots ring out.

adaptationNote: The chart’s KILL / SPARE / LET CROWD DECIDE (each with the cross-chapter padlock), offered with the template’s buttons in its order: REVENGE, SPARE, DON'T DECIDE (the option IDs keep the earlier scene’s meaning: 0 spare, 1 kill, 2 crowd). Arrows: REVENGE {{North}} small up (the template); SPARE and DON'T DECIDE none. The public-opinion change for killing the officers comes in the news afterwards (next scene). The crowd always kills them when {{Markus}} does not decide (wiki Note). The officer’s plea and the androids’ demands are the template’s; nobody argues for mercy, and {{Josh}} is not in the park. Changed from the earlier scene: no {{Josh}} or {{North}} speeches, no {{Josh}} arrows, no {{North}} down for sparing (none has a source), and the spared officers are not said to run for their car (the news finds them “in a state of shock”). Recorded for later chapters as capitolOfficers and capitolChrisDead (Meet Kamski, Freedom March).
